title: Failsafe route composer — UX walkthrough and backlog notes
content:
Purpose:
Quick internal walkthrough of a proposed ‘Failsafe Route Composer’ UI for the Rollouts console. The composer should make it easy for product engineers to declare primary routing logic (canary / A/B / weighted) plus deterministic fallback branches (region failover, model-variant fallback, capacity-tier degrade). This doc captures initial wireframe notes, step flows, suggested microcopy, edge cases, and an initial groomed backlog for implementation.

High-level goals:
- Let engineers express multi-stage fallbacks as a tree rather than flat chained policies.
- Keep the primary control surface simple: stepper + visual tree + compact rule editor.
- Make resilience explicit (show estimated RPO/RTO implications, cost delta hints).
- Provide a ‘simulate’ sandbox to preview request routing for sample traffic.

Mental model for users:
- Compose routes from left-to-right steps: Entry -> Split (ratio/criteria) -> Target -> Fallbacks -> Final catch-all.
- Each node can have metadata: model variant, region, capacity class, priority, timeout, circuit-breaker policy.
- Fallbacks are evaluated depth-first for a request; nodes show probability and expected latency band.

Wireframe notes (key screens / components):
1) Composer canvas (center)
   - Visual tree view, drag-to-connect nodes. Nodes are compact cards: title, small tag (region/model/capacity), latency badge, cost ballpark.
   - Top-left stepper: [Define entry] -> [Split rules] -> [Targets & fallbacks] -> [Policy settings] -> [Preview & save]
   - Top-right sticky summary: expected p99 latency, token-cost estimate, current canary percent, active feature flags.

2) Node inspector (right panel)
   - Editable fields: name, model (dropdown; supports pinned versions), region (multi-select), capacity tier, timeout-ms, retry-policy, circuit-breaker threshold.
   - Quick presets: "Low-latency" (prioritize region/fast variant), "Cost saver" (use quantized variant first), "Safe fallback" (strict degradation).
   - Microcopy: "Fallbacks run only if the parent target responds with 5xx, timeout, or KV-cache-miss and retry budget is available."

3) Split rule editor (modal)
   - Options: simple weight slider; audience criteria (header, cookie, user attribute), latency-based cutover (if median > X ms route to fallback), failure-rate threshold.
   - Visual preview of sample split (pie chart + table of sample requests).

4) Preview / simulate panel
   - Inputs: sample header set, mock client region, load (qps), seed for deterministic sample.
   - Output: step-by-step routing trace for N requests, showing which node each request hit and fallback triggers.
   - Button: "Export sample traces" (CSV).

Interaction flows (happy path):
- User chooses "New Failsafe Route" -> Stepper starts -> add Entry name + description -> Add Split node: set 10% canary to model-v2 in us-west -> Add Primary target: model-v1 us-east -> On Primary add fallback: model-v1-quantized us-east (cost saver) -> On top-level add region fallback: model-v1 eu-west -> Policy settings: setup circuit-breaker 10% failures in 60s -> Preview sim for 100 requests -> save as draft -> roll out with canary target at 10%.

Edge cases and error states:
- Detect loops (target A falls back to B which falls back to A) -> show validation error and highlight cycle.
- Conflicting policies: per-node timeout shorter than parent retry strategy -> show warning and suggested fix.
- Missing catch-all: if no final node covers 100% of requests, warn and require explicit confirm to allow rejects.
- Confusing weight sums: if sibling weights don’t add to 100, show normalized preview but badge suggests: "Weights normalized at save".

Observability and telemetry hooks (UX needs):
- Each node should expose a link to live metrics (p50/p90/p99 latency, 5xx rate, QPS) and config snapshot id.
- When previewing, surface the historical metric snapshot used to estimate latencies (timestamp + model version).
- Companion tooltip: "This estimate is based on last 24h data from the selected region and hardware type."

Suggested microcopy (small but important):
- Save CTA: "Save & stage rollout" (not just Save)
- Danger CTA on delete node: "Delete node and all dependent fallbacks"
- Preview CTA: "Simulate routing with sample traffic"

Acceptance criteria (MVP for UX handoff):
- Composer canvas implemented with add-node, connect, rename, and delete.
- Node inspector with model, region, timeout, and fallback list editable.
- Split editor supports weight and header-based audience rule.
- Validation: cycles, missing catch-all, weight normalization warnings.
- Preview sim returns deterministic routing for seed inputs and exports CSV.
- Unit tests for core UI components + E2E happy path (create -> save draft -> simulate).

Backlog (initial grooming) — rough estimates (T-shirt):
- PRD doc + API contract sketch (ENG-1298) -> owner: Marco -> small (2w)
- Canvas basic UI + node create/delete -> owner: frontend -> M (1w)
- Node inspector + presets -> owner: frontend/product -> M (1w)
- Split editor + audience rules -> owner: frontend/eng -> L (2w)
- Preview simulator backend + CSV export -> owner: backend -> L (2–3w)
- Validation rules and UX tooling hints -> owner: frontend -> S (4d)
- Telemetry links + metric snapshots integration -> owner: observability -> L (2w)
- QA + accessibility pass (keyboard navigation for canvas) -> owner: s/reliability -> M (1w)

Unresolved questions / TODOs:
- Should fallbacks consume retry budget from parent or have their own independent budget? (ops/eng input required)
- How do we present cost deltas for nested fallbacks without overwhelming the user? consider collapsed "cost impact" view.
- Are model variants allowed to be cross-region (pinning a variant to region only vs global variants)? needs infra constraints.
- Need product decision on whether normalized weights should be auto-adjusted or blocked at save.

Notes-to-self (informal):
- Meet with infra on 2025-02-18 re: cross-region pinned variants — add to ENG-1298 backlog.
- Add quick keyboard shortcuts for common actions: N = new node, D = duplicate node, / = search models.
- Consider a small onboarding microflow for first-time composer users (tooltip coach).

Related comps/refs (for visual inspiration):
- Draft canvas from Solutions Eng (see PR link above) — copy colors sparingly.
- Canary UI in older console: keep consistent stepper behavior but add tree visualization.

Owner notes for review: please scan validation section and backlog. I'm intentionally keeping the first iteration conservative (no auto-optimizations) — want a deterministic, explainable composer before adding "auto-fallback tuning" features.

End.
